item.text: I’m splitting the current combined options class into two real collaborators now: one to declare/register CLI options, and one to turn parsed options into a `ProjectGenerationRequest`. I’ll keep the handler thin and preserve all existing CLI behavior.

I’ve settled on the split: `InitCommandOptionDefinitions` will own the `OptionSpec` declarations and helper wiring, and `InitProjectGenerationRequestFactory` will own the parsed-to-request translation. That keeps parsing, declaration, and request assembly in separate classes instead of one combined utility.
I’m wiring the handler over to the new split collaborators now and removing the old combined `InitCommandOptions` dependency entirely. This should leave `InitOptionHandler` as orchestration only.

I’ve hit the main integration point. I’m fixing a likely type mismatch in the option-definition getters now, then I’ll add a focused test around the new request factory so the split stays covered independently.
I’ve finished the code split and I’m adding a direct factory test now. That keeps the new `InitProjectGenerationRequestFactory` covered without relying only on the full command integration path.
I’m doing the dependency sweep now. The last thing I want is a compile break from stale references after renaming the options layer.
I found one compile issue in the new factory test: I imported the wrong `OptionHandler` type. I’m fixing that and then I’ll do a final pass for formatting and stale references.
I’m doing the final validation pass now: stale-reference sweep and diff-check on the new split classes and test. If there’s a remaining issue, it should show up there.
The split is clean and the stale-reference sweep came back empty. I’m grabbing line references for the three new touchpoints so I can summarize the modular boundary precisely.
I found one leftover compile break in the new test: an incorrect `joptsimple.OptionHandler` import. I’m removing that now and then I’ll do one last check.
I’m running the final style/reference check now. If this is clean, the split is complete: definitions, factory, handler, and an isolated test for the new factory.

Split `InitCommandOptions` into two focused classes and updated the handler to compose them.

- `InitCommand` now wires together `InitCommandOptionDefinitions` and `InitProjectGenerationRequestFactory` instead of carrying option state itself. - `InitCommandOptionDefinitions` owns all CLI option declarations and exposes the parsed option handles. See [InitCommandOptionDefinitions.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/G004_spring_boot/cli/spring-boot-cli/src/main/java/org/springframework/boot/cli/command/init/InitCommandOptionDefinitions.java#L35-L224).
- `InitProjectGenerationRequestFactory` owns the translation from `OptionSet` to `ProjectGenerationRequest`. See [InitProjectGenerationRequestFactory.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/G004_spring_boot/cli/spring-boot-cli/src/main/java/org/springframework/boot/cli/command/init/InitProjectGenerationRequestFactory.java#L35-L86).
- Added a focused test for the new factory.
